newsitem.title: JAPAN: Toyota to use new lead-free wire harness.
newsitem.headline: Toyota to use new lead-free wire harness.

text.p: Japan's largest car maker Toyota Motor Corp will later this year start using lead-free wire it developed together with three cable makers, Toyota and the cable makers said on Wednesday.
The lead-free wire harness would help car makers reduce their use of lead, which is environmentally unfriendly, the four companies said in a joint statement.
The cable makers are Sumitomo Electric Industries Ltd, Furukawa Electric Co Ltd and Yazaki Corp.
By the end of 1998, Toyota would have replaced all its wire harness with the lead-free type, the statement said.
A compact car contains about 1.5 to two kg of lead, on top of the six kg in a car battery. Wire harnesses account for 150-200 grams of the total.
